basis: Developmental impairment and cleft palate are frequent; pharyngeal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Cardiac, renal, hearing and immune defects are occasional.
Multisuture craniosynostosis; hydrocephalus and hindbrain herniation are defining neurologic complications. Frequency of damaging corneal involvement is unclear.
Inherited platelet aggregation and clot retraction disorder; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate organ damage.
Acquired clonal blood disorder with complement-mediated hemolysis; characteristic disease-related thrombosis affects approximately 30-40% over untreated courses.
Ocular dysgenesis and skeletal abnormalities define WMS3; pulmonic stenosis affects 5/12 and aortic stenosis 4/12 patients.
Congenital digital skeletal malformations, including triphalangeal thumbs, brachydactyly and ectrodactyly.
Degenerative axial myopia directly damages ocular structures through staphyloma and chorioretinal degeneration.
Both listed subtypes cause brain disease or neurodegeneration; dysosteosclerosis belongs to the uncommon recessive subtype.
Aspartoacylase deficiency causes metabolic leukodystrophy with developmental impairment; retinal dystrophy is occasional, below 30%.
Type B1 brachydactyly is defined by distal phalangeal hypoplasia or aplasia with corresponding nail hypoplasia or absence.
Systemic inflammatory rheumatic syndrome; transient exanthema, arthralgia and reactive leukocytosis do not establish skin, joint or blood damage.
Loss of temporal comprehension is a higher cortical perceptual dysfunction.
Tumour originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no qualifying direct involvement of another organ is established.
Excess lacrimation is a disorder of the lacrimal apparatus.
Acute myeloid leukemia originates in marrow myeloid cells; KRAS mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
PPCS deficiency impairs coenzyme A biosynthesis and causes dilated cardiomyopathy, present in 5/5. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
Benign neoplasm directly occupies the endocardium.
Hereditary cutaneous hyperpigmentation; no additional organ disorder is documented.
Ventricular tachycardia is a cardiac electrical rhythm disorder.
Breast-associated syndrome of nonspecific systemic complaints; the definition does not establish direct inflammatory, neurologic or musculoskeletal organ disease.
Infection-associated fetal inflammation of the umbilical cord includes umbilical vessel inflammation; the vascular component falls within cardiovascular.
Facial lipoma is a benign adipose tissue tumour, usually in subcutis; conjunctival involvement is a specific subtype.
Rubella virus infection; its short-lived rash does not constitute lasting skin damage. Congenital organ defects belong to congenital rubella syndrome.
Spastic paraplegia with motor axonal neuropathy and intellectual disability; structural pes cavus occurs in 80-99%.
Digital and oral malformations define the syndrome. Corpus callosum agenesis affects 2/4 and atrioventricular canal defect 2/5; anal atresia affects 2/4.
